[USER] User is interested in how Wikipedia addresses conflicting information presented by multiple users.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Wikipedia relies on editing policies and guidelines, such as the "Neutral point of view" and "Verifiability," to handle conflicting information.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The "neutral point of view" guideline requires that article content must be written from a neutral perspective.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The "verifiability" policy requires that any information or claims made in an article must be backed up by reliable sources.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Wikipedia editors are responsible for resolving conflicting information by reviewing sources and ensuring content reflects a neutral point of view.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] If there is still disagreement, editors may seek input from other users or use a dispute resolution process.  
[USER] User expresses understanding of the assistant's explanation by saying, "That makes sense!"  
[USER] User inquires about tracking changes made to a Wikipedia article.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Wikipedia allows users to track changes through a feature called "Page history."  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Users can access the page history by clicking on the "View history" tab at the top of any Wikipedia article.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Page history feature shows a list of all changes made to an article, including who made the change, when, and what specific changes were made.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Page history helps users identify areas where conflicting information may have been added.  
[USER] User expresses surprise about the "Page history" feature.
